questions.q: What is Priya's specific worry heading into this project?
options: That the app's color scheme is outdated
That one VM remains a single point of failure right before the highest-traffic stretch of the year
That Casey will be hard to work with
That Terraform costs too much money
questions.explain: Priya is worried about reliability specifically ahead of Driftwood's Spring collection launch, about ten weeks out.

options: That the app is too fast
That infrastructure keeps being built as one-off, undocumented systems only Theo can rebuild
That Priya is too involved
That the storefront app needs a redesign
questions.explain: Casey wants systems describable in code and rebuildable by anyone, not dependent on one person's memory of manual steps.

questions.q: Why does Theo conclude the two stakeholders' priorities aren't actually in tension?
options: Because Priya and Casey agreed to compromise on half of each ask
Because each of the four deliverables turns out to serve both reliability and repeatability at once
Because Casey's ask was dropped entirely
Because the project was split into two separate unrelated projects
questions.explain: Laid out side by side, containers, Terraform, CI/CD, and the AWS backup target each serve both Priya's and Casey's concerns.

questions.q: What two things does Theo's scope document explicitly rule OUT of this project?
options: Containerizing the app and writing Terraform
Migrating any part of the app to AWS, and multi-region failover inside Azure
Building a CI/CD pipeline and adding monitoring
Talking to Priya and talking to Casey
questions.explain: The scope document names AWS migration and Azure multi-region failover as explicitly out of scope for this project.

questions.q: How does Terraform serve Priya's reliability concern specifically, according to the table in this lesson?
options: It makes the app run faster
It lets infrastructure be rebuilt quickly from code after a bad change
It eliminates the need for a CI/CD pipeline
It automatically fixes application bugs
questions.explain: Because the infrastructure is described in code, a bad change can be undone by rebuilding from that code, not by manual recovery.
